subject.title: Bug: exec() tool strips dollar-variable patterns via undocumented template substitution

question: Should Windows exec treat PowerShell `$...` expansion commands as supported one-shot approval candidates, or should OpenClaw keep rejecting that syntax and document the limitation?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but choosing between command-fidelity support and a documented security-boundary rejection changes Windows approval behavior for existing users.

options.title: Support With One-Shot Approval
options.body: Adopt the candidate direction once real Windows/Gateway proof shows `$...` commands reach explicit one-shot approval without auto-review or hanging.

options.title: Document Unsupported Syntax
options.body: Keep rejecting PowerShell expansion syntax in host approval analysis and update public exec docs with the supported script-file or command-shape workaround.

options.title: Defer For More Repro Data
options.body: Leave this issue open with the current needs-info state until a live Windows run proves the exact stripping behavior reported by users.

recommendation.title: Support With One-Shot Approval
recommendation.body: Adopt the candidate direction once real Windows/Gateway proof shows `$...` commands reach explicit one-shot approval without auto-review or hanging.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the current Windows shell analyzer and command authorization planner that this decision would modify.
